== Biography ==
'''John Glasgow''' was born about 1832 or 1833 in County Antrim, Ireland. The surviving 1851 census calls him an eighteen-year-old son of [[Glasgow-2981|James Glasgow]]. John was a linen weaver and was temporarily absent elsewhere in County Antrim when the Ballycregagh household was enumerated.<ref name="Census1851">1851 Census of Ireland, County Antrim, Dunaghy parish, Ballycraigargh, household 29, James Glasgow household: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G94X-YD22 living household, image 251] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L94X-Y621 continuation and mortality return, image 252].</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-2981]] is assessed at 99% (proved). The held 1851 Ballycregagh return expressly records eighteen-year-old John as James’s son, temporarily absent elsewhere in County Antrim. That is a direct paternal statement for the census-defined child, regardless of uncertain maternity or later adult identity.

Held 1851 census relationship quotation/summary and existing source citations establish the census-defined child’s father; no fresh image inspection or adult identity extension.

Next useful test: Inspect John’s original relationship line and later marriage for continuity.

Source basis already held: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G94X-YD22 1851 Census of Ireland, County Antrim, Dunaghy parish, Ballycraigargh, household 29, James Glasgow household: living household, image 251 (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G94X-YD22) and continuation and mortality return, image 252 (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L94X-Y621).]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.



=== Parentage ===

The census directly proves James as John's father. [[Hamilton-25516|Peggy Hamilton]] remains attached as an uncertain working mother because no better-supported replacement profile has been identified. Peggy and James reported marrying in 1848, about fifteen years after John's birth, so Peggy should not be treated as his proved mother. The marriage year alone does not make earlier biological maternity impossible. [[Unknown-764460|Mary Glasgow]] of the closely matching 1847 Glenleslie workhouse family is the stronger candidate, but that record does not include John and no record inspected so far explicitly calls him her son.

The [https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/census-record/#census_year=1851&surname__icontains=Glasgow&county=Antrim&limit=30&id=27846 National Archives of Ireland household link] already cited on the profile is preserved.
